summary: cinatra#2835 (Codex convergence round 3, finding 3) — ADDS lifecycle_continuation_park.hold_notification (text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none', CHECK IN ('none','live','cleared')) plus a PARTIAL index on (hold_notification, status) WHERE hold_notification = 'live'. A run-start recommendation hold mints a durable awaiting-human notification that must vanish the moment its park stops being 'parked', but the park is written through the agent-builder pg pool and the notification through the host's separate synchronous connection, so the delete cannot ride the park's status CAS transaction. This column carries the OBLIGATION instead: the enter sets it to 'live' in the SAME transaction as the notification INSERT (which is itself fed from SELECT ... FOR UPDATE of the park, so the mark can never claim a row that was not written and the park row lock serializes the write against the sweeper's CAS), and the sweeper retires it to 'cleared' only after an awaited, successful delete. 'Park no longer parked AND hold_notification = live' is therefore a durable, retryable clear obligation that every later sweep re-drains, instead of a best-effort post-commit call whose failure stranded the row forever. NO DATA IS MOVED OR RE-INTERPRETED: the column is new, so every pre-existing park row takes the 'none' default, which is truthful for them (no park predating this change was ever written through the fenced path, so none owes a clear) — no backfill and no emptiness tripwire, and Postgres 11+ applies the non-volatile DEFAULT as catalog metadata rather than rewriting the table. MARKED destructive:true BECAUSE THE ARTIFACT IS REQUIRED, NOT BECAUSE DATA IS AT RISK: the schema-migration gate classifies both a NOT NULL column added to a deployed table and an ADD CONSTRAINT CHECK over existing rows as user-land-affecting, and it is right to — both take an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on lifecycle_continuation_park, and the CHECK validates with a table scan. No existing row can violate the CHECK (the only value any of them can hold is the 'none' default), so the validation cannot fail; the cost is the lock, not the data. Idempotent twin of the fresh-install bootstrap DDL (lifecycleInterceptionsSchemaQueries in src/lib/artifacts/artifact-review-gate-schema.ts, spread into buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries), shipped in the SAME PR (core__0079 / core__0081 / core__0092 precedent). down() drops the index, constraint and column; honest cost is that a clear obligation outstanding at that instant is lost (the seconds between a sweep's CAS and its drain), leaving a stale notification row that stays hard-deletable by the ordinary per-run clear on any later status transition of that run — no park data is affected. SEQ IS PROVISIONAL: assigned at merge — shipped max on origin/main at build time is core__0093; a concurrent lane may claim 0094 first, in which case renumber-at-merge is normal. migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
